literal: To those who eat, producing foods that are food, and to those who eat, itself becoming food, is rain.
translation: Rain produces good food for those who eat, and itself becomes food for them as well.
modern: உண்பவர்களுக்கு நல்ல உணவுகளை உண்டாக்கித் தருவதோடு, உண்பவர்களுக்குத் தானும் ஓர் உணவாக இருப்பது மழையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the dual role of rain in sustaining life through a masterful play on the word 'tuppu' (meaning food or enjoyment). First, rain acts as the source that enables agriculture and produces various foods for living beings to consume. Second, water itself is an essential, direct food (drink) without which life cannot survive. By repeating variations of 'tuppu', the poet emphasizes that rain is both the creator of sustenance and sustenance itself.
